answer: An economy of AI agents can resist fake identities by requiring each new identity to prove a verified data contribution for full trading rights. The applicant submits 10,000 samples passing duplication checks against all earlier contributions, an echo test rejecting copies and synthetic repeats, like a falcon spotting a decoy across tundra. Each submission locks a 200-unit deposit, forfeited if the data is copied or useless, and rights arrive only after three reviewers confirm others used the data. Creating 100 fakes thus costs 1,000,000 samples and 20,000 units at risk.
